variants.name: Centered
variants.description: One column. Headline, lead and actions centre on the page and the media column is gone at every width.
variants.guidance: Sits at the top of the page, above the logo rail. Best for a launch, a manifesto or a developer tool whose proof is the install line rather than a screenshot. Avoid it when you have a real interface to show, because a centered hero with no media leaves the fold empty and the split layout exists for that. Pairs with marquee-ticker and stats-band directly beneath it.

variants.name: Media top
variants.description: The product panel moves above the copy at every width and the copy underneath is capped to a prose measure instead of sharing a row.
variants.guidance: Sits at the top of the page. Best when the screenshot is the argument and the headline is the caption, which is the usual shape for an analytics or observability product. Avoid it when the panel needs more than about 16:9 of height, because the fold then holds media and nothing else. Pairs with feature-grid:three-up below, which carries the detail the hero no longer has room for.

variants.name: Terminal
variants.description: Keeps the split but replaces the product panel with the install sequence, so the right column is code rather than an interface.
variants.guidance: Sits at the top of the page for a developer tool. Best when the fastest proof is that the thing installs in one line and there is no dashboard worth showing yet. Avoid it on a page aimed at buyers rather than builders, because a shell prompt reads as documentation to everyone else. Pairs with marquee-ticker beneath and feature-grid:numbered-steps further down.

variants.name: Editorial
variants.description: Headline runs across the full measure in the serif face, a hairline closes it, and the lead breaks into two text columns underneath instead of sitting beside a visual.
variants.guidance: Sits at the top of a long-form or announcement page. Best when the argument is written rather than shown, such as a release essay or a positioning page. Avoid it when the lead is shorter than about forty words, because two columns of one sentence each read as a mistake. Pairs with callout-editorial and the editorial skin, and reads best at the default tracking, never tighter than -0.035em.

Build software that looks human, not generated.

The open UI library built for AI agents and design engineers. Pure native CSS, tokenized skinning, and zero cookie-cutter templates.

Every class an agent emits is checked against the real stylesheet before it ships, so a name that does not exist never reaches a pull request. Reset, tokens, base, components and utilities are separate layers, which means you can override any of it without a specificity fight.

variants.name: Signup form
variants.description: The button pair becomes one email field with the submit inside the group and a one line assurance under it, while the media column stays where it was.
variants.guidance: Sits at the top of a page whose next step is an account rather than a tour. Best when the product is self serve and the signup genuinely needs one field, so the fold ends on the thing the visitor came to do. Avoid it when the real form asks for a company, a seat count and a demo slot, because the hero then promises a shortcut that does not exist. Pairs with cta-band:inline-form at the foot of the page, which closes on the same single field.
